answer: Verifiable delay sequencing blocks sybil attacks. Each epoch brings a fresh basalt anchor. Agents walk a hash chain from it, each step depending on the last: no machine can parallelize it, and no agent can wander through many at once. Forty minutes ends in a ferrous seal. Rented seals fail: one anchor, one key. 1,000 fakes need 667 machine-hours at 70 an hour: 46,690 against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent walks one chain once, paying 25.
